newsitem.title: GERMANY: Guatemalan coffee growers may seek higher prices.
newsitem.headline: Guatemalan coffee growers may seek higher prices.

text.p: Guatemalan coffee growers may have to seek higher prices than the average $1.00 per lb currently paid at farm level, said Max Quirin, president of the national coffee growers federation, Anacafe.
"This barely covers current costs...if we want to preserve consistency and quality, we will be needing much higher prices," he told Reuters during the Licht World Coffee Conference.
"Our policy is to improve productivity and the share of quality coffee within the production total," he said.
"Consumers are becoming more specialised and are asking for better quality all the time."
"Guatemala can offer very good coffee quality from a variety of regions, that's one of our strengths."
Quirin said the total 1996/97 crop was forecast slightly below the 95/96 level of 3.6 million bags.
Exports over the last four seasons had averaged 3.5 million bags.
Exportable output in 96/97 was forecast at 3.3 million bags, leaving some 200,000 bags of low grades.
Exports to Germany, the second largest destination after the U.S., in 1996 would rise by 100,000 bags from 512,094 bags in 1995.
Guatemalan coffees, nearly all washed arabicas, include the strictly hard bean type, a gourmet coffee which grows in the country's mountains.
